local.explanation: Works on a project file on this computer, without login or server. Only project files (.json) are opened here, never data files.
local.dropHint: Drop a project file here, or open one.
local.onlyProjectFiles: {{file}} was not opened: only project files (.json) can be opened here, never data files.
local.notAProject: {{file}} is not a valid project file
local.migrated: The file was in format {{from}}; it will be saved in format {{to}}.
local.unsaved: Unsaved changes: download the project to keep them.
local.downloadToSave: This browser cannot write the file: save by downloading it.

grid.label: Mapping grid of table {{table}}
grid.keys: Arrows or Tab to move, Enter to edit (on Element: the path picker; F2 to type the path), Esc to cancel. On a group: Enter opens or closes it. A new row is saved once it has a role and an element.
grid.conflict: This object was changed elsewhere: the grid now shows the current project. Make your change again.

roles.title: Roles
roles.explanation: A role is a FHIR resource made from each record, such as Patient[0] or Observation[1]. Here you set its type, index, label and table, and see its named slices (added from the path picker); the rest of a role comes later.
roles.none: No roles yet: add one to start mapping.
roles.deleteWarning_one: {{count}} row uses this role: it will show an error until you choose another role.
roles.deleteWarning_other: {{count}} rows use this role: they will show an error until you choose another role.

field.resourceTypeHint: As in FHIR, for example Patient, Observation, Condition
field.label: Label

roles.noRowKey: The table has no row key yet, so the role gets no id rule: it is added with the row key.
roles.idRuleKept: The id rule follows the type, index and table while it is the default one.
roles.deleteSliceWarning_zero: No row writes to this slice.
roles.deleteSliceWarning_one: {{count}} row writes to this slice: it will show an error until you change its path.
roles.deleteSliceWarning_other: {{count}} rows write to this slice: they will show an error until you change their paths.

validation.fhirChecked: Checked against FHIR {{version}}, as in cindermed validate.
validation.fhirOtherVersion: FHIR checks not run: the definitions are for FHIR {{index}}, the project for FHIR {{project}}. Write them again with cindermed fhir-index.
validation.fhirUnavailable: FHIR checks not run: write the definitions with cindermed fhir-index <project> --out apps/web/.fhir-index.
validation.fhirNotRun: FHIR checks not run: the project does not match the schema.
validation.failed: The check failed: {{message}}. It runs again after your next change.

details.noCell: Select a cell to see its findings.

findings.title: All findings
findings.none: No findings: the project passes every check.

picker.title: Element
picker.unknownType: {{type}} is not a resource type of the project's FHIR version.
picker.keys: Up and Down to move, Right to open, Left to close, Enter to choose. Complex types open when you need them; the search finds the opened ones. On a repeating element, name a repetition to write to it apart from the others.
picker.noRole: Choose the row's role first: the element tree depends on it.
picker.unavailable: No FHIR definitions in the browser: type the path, or write them with cindermed fhir-index.

slices.explanation: A named slice is one repetition of {{element}}, told apart from the others by a fixed value. Rows write to it with its name, and it is created only when one of them has a value.

field.name: Name
field.nameHint: Letters, digits and '-', starting with a letter: {{example}}

slices.manual: The code is saved as entered by hand: it is not checked against a terminology server.
slices.noDiscriminator: {{element}} has no child with a code or simple value to tell its repetitions apart.

error.nameInvalid: The name can hold letters, digits and '-', and starts with a letter.
error.nameTaken: The role already has a slice with this name on this element.
error.discriminatorRequired: Choose the element that tells the repetitions apart.
error.valueInvalid: The value is not of the element's type.
